test_title: PYST 39: RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I - GA (Held On: 29 Aug, 2025 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: What was the significant change in funding norms for National Sports Federations (NSFs) announced by the Indian government in 2025?

options.text: Allocation of at least 20% of their annual budget toward junior and youth development programmes
Elimination of funding for foreign coaches in order to promote Indian coaches and youth development programmes
Reduction in financial assistance for training athletes

solution:
The correct answer is __**Allocation of at least 20% of their annual budget toward junior and youth development programmes.**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In **2025**, the **Indian government** introduced a significant change in the funding norms for **National Sports Federations (NSFs)** to emphasize grassroots development and youth engagement.
 
• The new policy mandated that **at least 20% of the annual budget** allocated to NSFs must be directed toward **junior and youth development programmes**.
 
• This initiative aimed to nurture talent from an early age and ensure a **strong pipeline of athletes** for the future. This step focuses on building a foundation for competitive sports in India. *Hence, the correct answer is option 1.*
 
• The change aligns with the government’s broader vision of improving India’s **global sports performance** by investing in youth and grassroots-level sports infrastructure.
 
• While other options focused on reducing foreign coach expenses or decreasing financial assistance, the emphasis on youth development highlights the government’s commitment to long-term sports excellence. *Other options are incorrect as they do not align with the announced norms.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **National Sports Federations (NSFs) in India:**

 
 
• **NSFs** are responsible for the development, regulation, and promotion of various sports disciplines in India. They work in collaboration with the **Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports**.
 
• These federations play a crucial role in organizing national and international tournaments, nurturing talent, and providing infrastructure and training facilities for athletes.
 
 
 
• **Focus on Junior and Youth Development:**
 
 
• Investing in **junior and youth programmes** ensures that young athletes receive exposure to professional training and facilities at an early stage, thus fostering talent for international competitions.
 
• Such initiatives are essential to achieve long-term goals, such as improving India’s ranking in the **Olympics and global tournaments**.
 
 
 
• **Government’s Role in Sports Development:**
 
 
• **Sports Authority of India (SAI)** and NSFs receive funding from the government to enhance sports infrastructure and support athletes.
 
• Policies like these encourage federations to focus on grassroots-level development, which is critical for nurturing future champions.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Budget Allocation:**

 
 
• The mandate to allocate **20% of the annual budget** for junior and youth development is a progressive step, ensuring dedicated resources for nurturing young talent.
 
• This policy encourages NSFs to prioritize grassroots development over temporary measures like hiring foreign coaches.
 
 
 
• **Examples of Implementation:**
 
 
• **Khelo India Programme:** The government’s flagship initiative aimed at identifying and nurturing young talent aligns with this policy change.
 
• **State-Level Sports Academies:** Many state governments have already started implementing youth-centric sports academies to complement the NSF’s initiatives.
